ΔΔG for the JAK family: what exists, what we computed, and what it is worth

Four proteins, 87,343 substitutions, three ΔΔG methods plus RSA, measured against each other, against the clustering and against the one experimental dataset · 5 November 2026

Three ΔΔG methods cover these proteins completely, and they agree with each other only moderately. A single geometric number — relative solvent accessibility — tracks them nearly as well as they track each other, and beats all three at the job we actually use them for. The extreme-value tail that disfigures our PyRosetta numbers turns out to be largely a PyRosetta artefact, and the proline part of it entirely so.

1. What methods exist

familymethodsnote
force fieldFoldX, Rosetta ddg_monomer, Rosetta cartesian_ddgcartesian_ddg is most robust to modelling error
statistical potentialPoPMuSiC, mCSM, DUET, SDM, DDMutfast; graph / environment features
learned, structure-awareThermoMPNN, RaSP, Stability Oracle, SPURS, ThermoNettrained on mega-scale data
sequence / evolutionGEMME, EVE, TranceptEVE, ESM-2, ProSST, SaProtnot ΔΔG, but competitive on stability DMS
two-feature baselineRSALOR = log-odds ratio × RSAsee section 6
The field's real ceiling. On genuinely unseen single mutations the best methods reach r ≈ 0.5–0.6, not the 0.7–0.8 advertised — the gap is training-set leakage, direct+reverse evaluation, and random rather than homology-aware splits. Experimental noise caps the achievable value at r ≈ 0.7–0.8. For interpreting human missense variants ΔΔG is a weak classifier (AUC ≈ 0.66–0.68), because many pathogenic variants do not act by destabilisation. And there is no benchmark on large multi-domain proteins — which is what the JAKs are. Sources, with DOIs, in external_data/ddg_literature.md.

JAK1 and TYK2 were computed in October on four molab CPU boxes (20 cores each) overnight; JAK2 and JAK3 in November locally, in the times above.

Did we reproduce RSA or RSALOR? No — and that matters for how sections 6 and 8 should be read.

RSA is the exposure_rasa column of the downloaded ThermoMPNN file. We never ran a solvent-accessibility calculation ourselves. Every RSA number in this report rests on someone else's computation, on structures we did not choose.

RSALOR: data/ddg/rsalor_jak2_family.csv exists with the right columns (RSA, LOR, RSA*LOR, CI, pLDDT), but no script in this repository generates it and the package is not installed. It came from outside the repo or from a session that left no code. Its provenance is unverified, and it covers JAK2 only.

So the RSA findings below are: a downloaded RSA column behaves this way. They are consistent with the published RSALOR result, which is reassuring, but they are not an independent reproduction of it.

4. How the methods agree

The ΔΔG methods agree only moderately — Rosetta against the other two at 0.52–0.56, FoldX against ThermoMPNN at 0.69–0.70. The figure above shows the same pattern in all four proteins, to ±0.03.

Now read the RSA row against the Rosetta row. RSA correlates with ThermoMPNN at 0.59; PyRosetta — a full force-field calculation costing ~1.5 h per protein — correlates with the same ThermoMPNN at 0.54. The free number does better.

ddg_delta is flat against everything (|ρ| ≤ 0.02), as it is against the clustering and the DMS.

Three separate conclusions.

ThermoMPNN has no tail at all — 0.0% for all twenty residues. A bounded neural-net output cannot produce a −2,900 kcal/mol value, so the comparison is partly unfair; but it does establish that the tail is not a property of the substitutions themselves.

FoldX reproduces the aromatic ranking — W, Y, F are its top three (14.1 / 11.0 / 7.0%). So the steric mechanism is real: forcing a large aromatic into a packed core genuinely clashes.

FoldX does not reproduce proline — 2.5% against Rosetta's 92.5%. That part is a backbone-geometry failure specific to our protocol: mutate_residue with an 8 Å repack does not re-sample the backbone, and proline's ring constrains φ, so a proline forced into a non-proline backbone registers an enormous clash that relaxation would relieve.

Practical consequence: winsorise or rank-transform the Rosetta ΔΔG before use, and do not interpret raw X→P values at all.

6. RSA, and the two-feature baseline

Tsishyn, Pucci & Rooman, Bioinformatics 2025 — RSALOR (10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf322). Two features — log-odds ratio from an MSA × relative solvent accessibility — benchmarked on ProteinGym (~700,000 mutations, 218 DMS sets) against 27 predictors including 19 protein language models. On the Stability slice: ProSST-2048 0.638, SaProt 0.565, RSALOR 0.551, ESM2-650M 0.496, −RSA alone 0.480, conservation alone 0.447 (Spearman).

RSA alone beats ESM2-650M on stability, and the two-feature model beats most deep models. Our numbers reproduce the shape of that result on the JAKs independently.

We have RSALOR output for JAK2 already (data/ddg/rsalor_jak2_family.csv) but have not yet used it as a clustering feature. It is the clearest cheap improvement available.

RSA beats every ΔΔG method on every protein — AUC 0.765–0.816 against 0.711–0.791 — and it is the cheapest quantity in the table. Note also that these AUCs are partly circular for FoldX and Rosetta, which are clustering features; RSA is not, and still wins.

The conservation-based predictors beat the stability methods at predicting measured protein abundance. Abundance is close to a direct readout of folding stability — exactly what ΔΔG computes — and AlphaMissense, which never sees a force field, is 60% better at it than PyRosetta.

RSA alone (0.288) beats both FoldX and Rosetta. Again — though see section 2: this is a downloaded RSA column, not one we computed.

In the methods' defence: these are single-point correlations over a whole multi-domain protein, the hardest possible setting, and the independent literature ceiling is r ≈ 0.5–0.6 on curated single-domain sets. 0.26–0.30 is poor but not anomalous.

9. Recommendations

  1. Do not use ddg_delta. Inert on four proteins; on JAK2 it also fails to reproduce between two model pairs (r = 0.074).
  2. Winsorise Rosetta ΔΔG and drop X→P values.
  3. Add RSA as a feature. Free, already present at 100% coverage, and it outperforms all three ΔΔG methods.
  4. Consider replacing Rosetta with ThermoMPNN in the feature set: better AUC, better agreement with FoldX, no outlier tail, no 1.5 h per protein, 100% coverage. Keep Rosetta for the dual-state question it was computed for.
  5. Try RSALOR properly — the JAK2 output is already on disk.
